evals.prompt: I run marketing at a small literary publisher. Our monthly email newsletter 'The Shelf' — a staff book pick, a list of new releases, and a short author interview — has slipped from 31% to 22% open rate over the past year and clicks are flat. Use SCAMPER to come up with ideas to make it fresh again, and tell me which ones to try first.
evals.expected_output: Full SCAMPER session: framed goal, attributes, ideas under all 7 letters with bold ideas, scored shortlist, prioritized next steps with tests.
expectations: Opens with an Assess line stating the goal, what to Keep vs Change, and an effort level
Presents 3 named variations (A/B/C) as drafted concepts (concept cards or draft copy), not only idea lists
M ideas include at least one Magnify and one Minify
Each recommendation has a riskiest assumption and a cheapest test
Addresses the open-rate problem specifically (subject line / sender / preview / timing)
Backlog of undrafted ideas is 8 items or fewer
Ends with a close: What changed table, recommendation, and a line saying whether drafts were visually checked

evals.prompt:
here's the back-cover blurb for a debut psychological thriller we're publishing in spring. it feels super generic. can you rework it? give me 3 rewritten options.

'Some secrets are better left buried. When Clara Hayes returns to her childhood home in the small coastal town of Wrenmouth after her mother's sudden death, she discovers a box of letters that will change everything she thought she knew about her family. As dark truths begin to surface, Clara must race against time to uncover the past before it destroys her future. A gripping, twisty page-turner you won't be able to put down.'
evals.expected_output: Three finished rewritten blurbs, each labelled with the SCAMPER operator(s) behind it, cliches removed, a recommendation.
expectations: Opens with an Assess line stating the goal, what to Keep vs Change, and an effort level
Shows the original blurb, then three complete rewritten blurbs ready to use
Each rewrite is labelled with a name and the SCAMPER letters behind it
None of the rewrites use 'better left buried', 'race against time', or 'put it down'
Invented plot specifics are flagged as placeholders
Ends with a close: What changed table, recommendation, and a line saying whether drafts were visually checked

Focuses on Eliminate and Reverse/Rearrange rather than a full 7-letter session
Proposes guest checkout / account after purchase
Shows at least one variation as a before -> after flow of checkout steps
Recommends testing/measuring the changes
Ends with a close: What changed table, recommendation, and a line saying whether drafts were visually checked

evals.prompt:
Here's our latest blog post. Can you repurpose it for social?

Why Your Book Club Keeps Falling Apart. Most book clubs don't end with a fight. They fade. Someone skips a month, then two, and the group chat goes quiet. In our survey of readers at our spring events, the most common reason people gave for quitting was not time, it was books they didn't enjoy. Three fixes help: let members take turns choosing, but cap picks at 350 pages; meet even when half the group hasn't finished, because the conversation is the point, not the homework; and end every meeting by agreeing the next date before anyone leaves. Clubs that set the next date in the room are far more likely to still be meeting a year later. Your book club isn't failing because people stopped loving books. It's failing because nobody owns the next step.
evals.expected_output: Reformat preset: keep message, change format; three drafts are three different formats in their native structure; no new claims.
expectations: Opens with an Assess line stating the goal, what to Keep vs Change, and an effort level
Reads it as reformat: message under Keep, format/channel under Change
The three drafts are three different social formats (e.g. carousel, thread, short video script), each written in its native structure (slides / posts / timed beats)
Thread draft (if any) has a first post that stands alone and posts within 280 characters if for X
Adds no factual claims or statistics that are not in the source post (e.g. does not invent a percentage for 'far more likely')
Ends with a close: What changed table, recommendation, and a line saying whether drafts were visually checked

evals.prompt: We have an infographic idea '7 steps to plan a book launch' that we made for publishers. Make it work for first-time self-published authors, in our brand style: navy #1B2A4A, coral #FF6F59, font Poppins. Keep the 7-step checklist structure.
evals.expected_output: Keep: 7-step structure. Change: audience, style. Drafts use brand colours/font and address self-published authors.
expectations: Opens with an Assess line stating the goal, what to Keep vs Change, and an effort level
Keep includes the 7-step checklist structure; Change includes audience and style
Every draft keeps exactly 7 steps
Visual drafts use #1B2A4A and #FF6F59 and the Poppins font
Copy addresses first-time self-published authors (e.g. no publicist/sales-team assumptions; mentions things like ISBN, retailers, ARC readers, budget)
Ends with a close: What changed table, recommendation, and a line saying whether drafts were visually checked
